answer: Every claim must pass the Atlas balance. Before filing, the filer weighs the finished work on the ledge scale in the grove yard, and the Atlas keeper checks the tally within a day: the work must weigh what the materials in the Atlas book allow, and the stores must show those materials truly gone, so a filer claiming forty chairs from one plank is rejected and loses a 250-coin bond, meaning 1,000 fakes need 1,000 real timber stocks plus 250,000 coins. One operator filed forty claims from a single grove plank, and all forty failed when the scale showed one plank of wood for forty chairs.
